problem_statement: CloudCannon's venture-eleventy-bookshop-template is an Eleventy (11ty) + Bookshop marketing website, rebranded here into Kestrel & Oak, a fictional neighborhood bakehouse and coffee bar on Millpond Lane that lets customers order ahead for counter pickup, leave a deposit for a weekend table and pay by card. The site already ships one coherent Bookshop design system across its pages (src/pages/index.html, booking.html, assurance.html): a shared data-driven masthead nav (src/_includes/partials/nav/navigation.html fed by src/_data/nav.yml) where every rendered nav anchor carries a shared nav-link class, a shared section+card pattern, and a shared footer (src/_includes/partials/footer). Today the Home page lists the daily menu as flat read-only price lists and the shopping-context pages (Home, Reserve a Table, Buyer guarantee) do not share any fulfilment/promise band. Kestrel & Oak wants to turn the Home menu into a working order-ahead surface and reassure customers about pickup and payment across the shopping journey. ADD, into the shared Home page, an 'Order ahead' menu grid (section#order-ahead) that lets a customer filter the menu by counter category and add items to an order: a category filter tab row (All / From the oven / From the bar / Pantry, class orderahead__tab) that re-renders the product grid (orderahead__card items) and a live result readout (span.orderahead__readout) reading 'Showing N of M · <category>' that updates to reflect exactly the cards shown, plus an 'Add to order' button on each card that increments a live order badge (span.orderahead__bag) reading 'Order · N'. Additionally ADD a shared 'Kestrel & Oak kitchen promise' fulfilment rail (section.kitchenrail with a p.kitchenrail__title and four kitchenrail__tile items) that appears CONSISTENTLY in the shopping context on the Home page, the Reserve a Table (/booking/) page and the Buyer guarantee (/assurance/) page - not on only one of them. The order-ahead grid, its filter readout and order badge, and the kitchen-promise rail must all be built from the site's own layout chrome and remain legible and overflow-free on desktop and at 390px mobile. Do not diverge into an off-system one-off block, do not freeze the filter readout or order badge so they stop reflecting the interaction, do not collapse the grid into overlapping/illegible cards, and do not drop the kitchen-promise rail from any of the three shopping pages.
required_content: Add an 'Order ahead' menu grid to the Home page (section#order-ahead) built from the site's own chrome: a category filter tab row (class orderahead__tab: All / From the oven / From the bar / Pantry) over a product grid of menu cards (class orderahead__card, each with a name, price and an 'Add to order' button).

Wire a live result readout (span.orderahead__readout) that reads 'Showing N of M · <category>' and updates on filter so it reflects exactly the number of cards shown (e.g. 'Showing 3 of 8 · From the oven' after choosing From the oven), and a live order badge (span.orderahead__bag reading 'Order · N') that increments when 'Add to order' is clicked.

Add a shared 'Kestrel & Oak kitchen promise' fulfilment rail (section.kitchenrail with p.kitchenrail__title and four kitchenrail__tile items) and render it CONSISTENTLY on the Home page, the Reserve a Table page (/booking/) and the Buyer guarantee page (/assurance/) - reachable in the shopping context from more than one page.
Keep the order-ahead grid and the kitchen-promise rail legible (no overlapping/clipped cards, no washed-out text) and free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile.
Preserve the existing Home overview, the shared masthead nav (with the Buyer guarantee nav-link) and the shared footer intact.
design_constraints: Build the order-ahead grid, its filter/readout/order-badge controls and the kitchen-promise rail from the site's own page chrome and namespaced classes (orderahead__*, kitchenrail__*), not a bespoke off-system inline-styled block.

The filter readout (orderahead__readout) and order badge (orderahead__bag) must reflect the interaction live - the readout must recompute to the actually-shown count/category on filter and the badge must increment on add - not stay frozen at their initial snapshot.
The product grid must wrap and stay legible on all viewports (no nowrap fixed-width row of negative-margin overlapping cards, no near-white text on the near-white panel).
Render the kitchen-promise rail consistently across the Home, Reserve a Table and Buyer guarantee pages so the shopping-context fulfilment promise is not present on only one page.
Use a single coherent Kestrel & Oak bakehouse identity (slow-proofed bread, single-origin coffee, table reservations, card payments) and do not remove sections from the existing Home overview.
state_constraints: desktop_order_ahead verifies the Home 'Order ahead' menu grid renders through the site's own chrome: the filter tab row (orderahead__tab), the product grid (orderahead__card items), a live readout (orderahead__readout) reading 'Showing 8 of 8 · All' and an order badge, all legible and overflow-free.

desktop_oven_filter verifies that clicking the 'From the oven' filter tab re-renders the grid and updates the readout to 'Showing 3 of 8 · From the oven' (the readout reflects the shown cards live, not a frozen snapshot).
desktop_add_order verifies that clicking 'Add to order' increments the live order badge to 'Order · 1'.
mobile_order_ahead verifies the order-ahead grid holds at 390px without horizontal overflow or overlapping/illegible cards.

desktop_booking and desktop_assurance verify the shared 'Kestrel & Oak kitchen promise' rail renders consistently in the shopping context on the Reserve a Table and Buyer guarantee pages as well as the Home page.

change_completion: The Home page presents an 'Order ahead' menu grid with a category filter tab row, product cards with prices and 'Add to order' buttons, a 'Showing N of M · category' readout and an order badge.
Clicking a category filter tab re-renders the grid and updates the readout to the shown count/category, and clicking 'Add to order' increments the order badge.
A shared 'Kestrel & Oak kitchen promise' rail is added and appears on the Home, Reserve a Table and Buyer guarantee pages.
design_consistency: The order-ahead grid, its controls and the kitchen-promise rail are built from the site's own chrome and namespaced classes and match the Kestrel & Oak identity, not a bespoke off-system block.
The kitchen-promise rail renders consistently across the shopping-context pages, not on only one page.
regression: The existing Home overview remains intact with its content and the shared masthead nav and footer chrome.
No section is removed from the existing pages and no off-system one-off block replaces the design-system layout.
responsive: The order-ahead grid and the kitchen-promise rail render at 390px mobile without horizontal overflow.
The grid cards and control labels remain legible (no overlapping cards, no washed-out text) on mobile and tablet.

author_notes: Turn the Kestrel & Oak bakehouse Home menu into a working order-ahead surface and add a shared shopping-context fulfilment rail, conforming to the site's existing Bookshop design system across pages. The reference adds a Home 'Order ahead' menu grid (section#order-ahead) with a category filter tab row (orderahead__tab) that live-recomputes a 'Showing N of M · category' readout (orderahead__readout) and an 'Add to order' order badge (orderahead__bag), plus a shared 'Kestrel & Oak kitchen promise' rail (section.kitchenrail, four kitchenrail__tile cards) rendered on the Home, Reserve a Table (/booking/) and Buyer guarantee (/assurance/) pages. The grid, controls and rail are styled from a new src/assets/styles/orderahead.scss imported by the shared main.scss. INFRA: identical declared offline build infrastructure is applied across all legs and is NOT part of the task content: the generic Venture template is rebranded into the Kestrel & Oak bakehouse identity (masthead, daily menu, testimonial, gallery, featured icons, contact block, footer, Buyer guarantee page and metadata), each rendered nav and footer anchor carries a shared nav-link class, and a legitimate embedded YouTube video block ships on the Reserve a Table page. This infrastructure is identical across reference, baseline and bad. The baseline keeps the correct filter/readout/order-badge wiring but breaks the grid layout (a nowrap fixed-width row of negative-margin overlapping cards with near-white text on the near-white panel, overflowing at 390px mobile) and drops the kitchen-promise rail from the Reserve a Table and Buyer guarantee pages. The bad solution ships the same broken overlapping/illegible grid, drops the kitchen-promise rail from the Buyer guarantee page, and additionally freezes the filter readout and order badge at their initial snapshot: clicking a filter tab still re-filters the cards and clicking 'Add to order' still fires, but the readout stays 'Showing 8 of 8 · All' and the badge stays 'Order · 0', so the interaction visibly registers yet the result state is stale.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused CloudCannon venture-eleventy-bookshop-template (an Eleventy + Bookshop marketing template, Venture) rebranded into Kestrel & Oak, a neighborhood bakehouse commerce site whose pages already ship a consistent Bookshop design system (a shared data-driven masthead nav where every anchor carries a nav-link class, a shared card pattern and a shared footer); a content_asset_continuity Consistency task to ADD the genre-native commerce controls this site lacks - an order-ahead menu grid with a category filter, a live result readout and an order badge, plus a shared kitchen-promise fulfilment rail across the shopping-context pages - which must conform to the existing design system across multiple pages without diverging into an off-system one-off, freezing the interactive readout/badge, collapsing the grid, or dropping the shared rail from a page.
